approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current session’s scored observations. It keeps the best 64 molecules, draws breeding parents from score quantiles, and constructs fresh candidates through connected-fragment crossover or successive random atom, bond and ring mutations. Ordinary mutation requests one, two or three calls, with occasional longer recovery walks after repeated construction failures; crossover has its own finishing mutation. Only the final product can enter the candidate pool, after stable molecular identity, duplicate and source-relative sulfur checks. A count-fingerprint Tanimoto Gaussian process fitted to the complete accepted archive then uses correlated posterior draws to choose the announced batch from the fresh pool. New real scores update both the archive and the breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled.
approach.novelty: Increase the chance of an ordinary two- or three-call walk at the normal floor of one, from 18% to 36%, using one fixed unguided distribution. This gives the existing operators more opportunities to construct combinations that a single admitted edit would miss, while preserving final-only admission and the inherited recovery schedule. The same-Parent removal control established that keeping occasional continuation helps under these conditions, but did not test increasing its frequency. This experiment changes that frequency alone. It adds neither the earlier losing two-arm posterior guidance rule nor intermediate-product admission, a broader pool or a new graph operator. Greater productive gain remains a hypothesis: extra calls could also erase useful first edits or consume work without delivering useful evaluated products.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is sparse productive ordinary continuation in a search whose local successes do not reliably translate into stronger endpoints. The actual n-1744a1494180 summary.json/run.log pairs are complete on all three supplied seeds: macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, with seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. A read-only recount of all fifteen published Parent task logs finds 41,688 ordinary attempts, 7,502 multi-call attempts and 8,742 successful optional second/third calls. Only 310 multi-call ordinary finals reached accepted evaluation, with 43 strict best-parent beats, 16 sequential incumbent improvements and 144 later breeding sources. Across all 4,350 accepted offspring the Parent has 648 best-parent beats and 255 incumbent improvements. No higher-floor attempt occurred; the maximum member-attempt count was six. The isolated current-Parent removal n-c070e95b09ef loses 0.03069975142490533 on the complete panel with all three seed macros lower, even while parent-beating and incumbent-update counts rise to 659 and 277. Its loss remains about 0.014089 in the separately reported fourteen-cell sensitivity. This supports continuation presence, not a positive derivative with respect to continuation probability or an optimum. The ungated removal n-dbee08307e86 and historical exchange-containing removal n-29d770e728a6 retain their own Parents; their losses are contextual support, not current-Parent replication. The different-Parent two-arm guidance n-87c89dda7e3b loses 0.04808254201485503 despite evaluated delivery and later breeding. The unanswered question is whether a fixed larger unguided share delivers useful magnitudes and descendants rather than merely more local events.

literature_review.conclusion: A fresh current search and primary article/code inspection found no useful source identifying an optimum for this exact floor-one requested-call law. I also read the private round-31 search-policy literature review; retain its fixed upward-direction decision and its rejection of fragment/database additions that would introduce another proposal mechanism. The recorded source nodes have no literature_review to reuse, so this review honestly records a new search. Adopt only the assigned [0.64,0.30,0.06] unguided variant, motivated principally by the complete current-Parent presence control and the explicit carried open question. Reject treating Jensen’s rates, Mol GA’s generation size, generic multi-mutation results, new models or the failed two-arm guidance as a validated schedule recipe. Extra productive construction, real accepted delivery and reuse are predictions to test, not literature guarantees. No sweep, heavier follow-on schedule or guidance combination is registered.

finding_summary.headline: More continuation reaches evaluated products and later descendants, but the full panel loses 0.03895
finding_summary.insights:
Keeping occasional continuation and increasing its frequency require different contribution claims. The earlier complete removal control lost endpoint score, while this fixed upward change also loses against the same Parent. Together they narrow the question: useful continuation presence does not establish that more continuation improves this search, and neither contrast locates an optimum or supports a schedule sweep. The longer-path channel clearly reaches labeled products, productive cores and real recursive ancestry, so the endpoint loss cannot be dismissed as failure to expose it. Its small pooled parent-relative gain increase also does not explain endpoint quality: gain rates decrease in eight of fifteen sessions and in the early and late phases, and absolute source and offspring quality are lower. One exposed session supplies fourteen affected finals and a real breeding draw but no accepted descendant; recursive delivery is conditional, not universal.

The chemistry assessment likewise finds broader core coverage without consistently credible alternatives: nitrogen-halogen observations increase from 786 to 1,398, and perceived cyclic cumulated-carbon observations from 6 to 159. Reactive substitution, difficult ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry remain alongside recognizable amides and amines. These concurrent chemical differences describe the produced graphs; they do not establish which extra call, scaffold or adaptive-history change caused the score loss. The evidence supports a negative incremental contribution of this upward probability variant under the frozen panel, while preserving the earlier positive presence finding. Higher-floor escalation, unlabeled alternate products, component mediation and the catalog’s separate attribution and publication gaps remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen sessions expose the changed ordinary schedule. There are 8,618 saved draws requesting one extra call, and every extra call succeeds. Successful optional calls per ordinary attempt rise from 0.2097 to 0.4168. Two- or three-call pool finals increase from 7,392 to 14,479, and evaluated ordinary multi-call finals from 310 of 2,860 to 669 of 2,888. The naturally affected cohort delivers 390 evaluated finals; 73 become actual parents of 308 later accepted offspring. These are observed products and descendants, while alternate or intermediate products remain unscored.

Positive gain over the original best generating parent per accepted ordinary product rises slightly, from 0.003979 to 0.004138. Ordinary offspring mean score nevertheless falls from 0.3859 to 0.3476, their best-source mean from 0.4515 to 0.4119, and strict parent beats from 448 to 442. Across all offspring, positive parent-gain mass falls from 17.25 to 15.55 and sequential incumbent-gain mass from 5.819 to 5.235. Productive new typed/generic cores among multi-call finals increase from 28/19 to 61/39. Thus more real longer paths and more productive cores coexist with weaker overall search trajectories.

The complete matched mean falls from 0.596453 to 0.557498, a change of -0.038955 against the required +0.002. Seed macro changes are -0.083591, -0.017451 and -0.015823; 12 of 15 endpoints decrease. Macro population standard deviation decreases from 0.033970 to 0.008909, which does not satisfy the gain claim. The Parent late breakthrough remains in the primary panel; even the separately reported fourteen-cell sensitivity loses 0.024008. Ordinary activation is confirmed and the endpoint-gain falsifier is triggered. Higher-floor rejection escalation receives zero natural exposure.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl amides, amines and polar heterocycles retain reactive nitrogen bonds, strained topology and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9d88f032c4dc produces fused aromatic amide/thioamide series, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, nitrogen/carbonyl medium-ring systems, and fluorinated imino/dicarbonyl structures with both aromatic and nonaromatic rings. These are substantial molecular graphs, rather than predominantly chains or tiny fragments. The digest ring-closure-string incidences span 0.9621 to 0.9851; aromatic-string incidence spans 0.7621 to 0.9782. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or geometric validation. Median heavy-atom count across accepted optimizer observations is Child 29 versus Parent 28, with median perceived ring count 4 in each. Multiple seed-specific families and 2087 distinct typed/1300 distinct generic Murcko core identities across the Child panel, versus Parent 1740/1016, support moderate structural diversity; the identity counts include the empty core and do not measure productive cores or chemically feasible alternatives. Leading series still often share one scaffold within a session. Some outputs have recognizable medicinal chemistry, particularly aryl cyclic amines and connected heteroaryl amides, but direct N-halogen bonds, N-S/N-O environments, small-ring unsaturation and dense fused/bridged connectivity make overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. There are 1398 Child optimizer observations with direct N-halogen bonds versus Parent 786; O-halogen observations are 111 versus 217, and sulfur-halogen observations 19 versus 93. These motif counts overlap and describe output under the inherited source-relative sulfur condition, not gate decisions or chemical safety. Sulfur-containing observations are 1530 versus 1100, so sulfur is well represented. RDKit perceives cyclic cumulated carbon centres in 159 Child observations versus Parent 6, concentrated in a fluorinated/polar family; ring alkynes are absent from Child observations versus Parent 13. Thus the residual geometry concerns change form rather than uniformly tracking one motif. All digest stereocentre-string and charge-string incidences are 0.0. Potential unassigned stereocentres occur in 2144 Child optimizer observations versus Parent 2455; this is a graph-perception count and does not establish configurational stability. Neutral notation coexists with available aliphatic amines and supplies no protonation-state measurement. All 15 Child and 15 authoritative published Parent trajectory paths were present and read: 900 records per objective per node, including 870 optimizer observations, for 4350 optimizer observations per node. No task, trajectory path or paired seed comparison is missing; context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile mismatch. The original Parent molecular report was read through the search-only published path supplied by context.evidence_index. Every cited complete SMILES is from the Child digest or a trusted Child trajectory; Parent chemistry comparisons use its published search trajectories without adding Parent-only SMILES to the citation list. The digest final_molecules excerpt is the last seed-2 proposal group, not the set of seed incumbents. Graph descriptions, observation counts and source hashes are recorded in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20261003/r31-slot3-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. RDKit 2023.09.6 was used read-only, with no oracle, synthetic-accessibility scoring or conformer validation. The score gradients below are associations among observed molecules. They do not identify a hidden target pharmacophore, predict labels for proposed alternatives, establish component attribution, decide mechanism activation or infer endpoint benefit.

per_task.generated_character: Seed leaders have 24-25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, including a fused aromatic five/six-membered system and a phenyl or pyridyl region. Seed 0 retains a methyl/vinyl-ether substituted indole-like aryl carboxamide with direct amide N-F and ring N-S-H substitution. Seed 1 instead favors an N-vinyl fused aromatic system joined to a pyridyl region through an amine, with methoxy and fluoromethyl groups. Seed 2 carries a thioamide, N-Cl/N-Br and ring N-OH. Median size is Child 25 versus Parent 24 heavy atoms. The aromatic/carbonyl skeletons are recognizable, while the reactive nitrogen substitution makes the leaders questionable as routine synthetic endpoints.
liabilities: Direct N-F/N-Cl/N-Br amide bonds and ring N-S-H or N-OH attachments require separate local stability and synthesis assessment; they are chemically different environments.
Large peroxide-linked elaborations and small floor-scoring fragments show that useful functional context is not preserved consistently.
missing_features: Conventional nitrogen substitution preserving the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is not consistently realized among the Child leaders; the close N-halogen-free example still carries N-S-H and imine chemistry.
Independent, synthetically credible realizations of the leading arrangement remain limited. These trajectories cannot specify an exact absent target pharmacophore.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
